dossier.public_summary: The 1.58-day dip is on the M dwarf but is very deep (~28% of the star, implying a star-sized companion) and V-shaped. Odd and even dips differ significantly, the depth changes between sectors, and individual transits are inconsistent. The period exactly matches the star's 1.58-day rotation with large spot signals, indicating a grazing eclipsing binary on the target, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even dips differ by 33 sigma, ~6% (~16060 ppm) shallower odd vs even, strong systematic binary at twice the period (3.16 d) evidence, not a planet
Extremely V-shaped grazing eclipse with depth 277300 ppm implies companion radius 28.94 Rearth (~0.53 Rs), not planet-sized, favors stellar eclipse
Dip period matches stellar rotation to within 0.01% with large variability amplitude, consistent with spot-modulated grazing binary / synchronous binary, counts with large chi2 shape
